solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Heart-rending depression ultimately ate into us (7)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: at the end, so take the final letter of each of the next two words

blocks.note: a pit is a depression in the ground

annotation.surface: Someone describes a gloomy mood that gnawed away at them, told with heart-rending pathos.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ate into' reads as one verb, but 'ultimately' is taking the tail letter from each of its two words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe something so sad it moves you to pity.

entries.clue: Show of approval from group of animals eating that bone frantically (3,2,3,4)

indicatorNotes.eating: whoever eats something takes it inside, so the pack holds the other letters
indicatorNotes.frantically: something done frantically is wild and disordered, so the letters of 'that bone' lose their order

blocks.note: a pack of wolves or dogs
anagram fodder, 8 letters, placed between P and ACK

annotation.surface: A pack of dogs tears frantically at a bone, somehow earning praise for it.
annotation.walkthrough: The pack splits after its first letter: P, then the shuffled letters, then ACK.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the physical gesture of patting someone's back stands for any expression of approval.

entries.clue: Computer processing speed changed after large operation (8)

indicatorNotes.changed: a word that has been changed is no longer as written, so the letters of 'after' are rearranged
indicatorNotes.after: the rearranged letters come first, then L and OP follow

blocks.note: L = large, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: A computer's speed has been different ever since it had a big repair job.
annotation.walkthrough: 'After' looks like a time word linking the halves, but it is the fodder for 'changed'.
annotation.definitionFit: A technical term: a teraflop is a trillion floating-point operations per second, a unit for computing speed.

entries.clue: Responsibility of old group of students (4)

blocks.note: the NUS is the National Union of Students in the UK

annotation.surface: A question of who is accountable for a former student society.
annotation.walkthrough: The National Union of Students represents British university and college students.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, from the Latin for 'burden': the duty that falls on someone.

entries.clue: School is on top of multiplication and division (6)

indicatorNotes.top of: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

blocks.note: sch. is an abbreviation for school

annotation.surface: A school is on top of its arithmetic, having mastered multiplication and division.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Multiplication and division' looks like a single phrase from a maths lesson, but it breaks at 'and': division alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of a split between factions, classically within a church.

entries.clue: Be careful how a cut possibly throbs initially (5,3)

indicatorNotes.possibly: what is possibly so is not fixed, so the letters could be arranged another way

blocks.note: first letter of 'throbs', added to the fodder

annotation.surface: A warning to take care, since a cut may start throbbing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'How' reads as part of the sentence but is fodder too; only the T comes from outside it.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are imperatives used as warnings, so each swaps for the other in 'Be careful!'.

entries.clue: Against books getting fed into AI (4)

indicatorNotes.getting fed into: NT goes inside AI, as data is fed into a model

blocks.note: taken as written, split to hold NT
NT = New Testament, a set of books

annotation.surface: A protest against books being used as training data for artificial intelligence.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Books' is the New Testament here, a crossword staple, not the novels the surface suggests.
annotation.definitionFit: A preposition in both cases: someone anti a plan is against it.

entries.clue: Sound broadcasting organisation (7)

blocks.note: not audio: a sound is a narrow stretch of sea between two coasts

annotation.surface: A description of a radio company, with 'sound' as in audio.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sound' reads as audio for radio, but it is the water sense: a strait such as the English Channel.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a sound and a channel are both narrow sea passages, and a channel is also a TV or radio station.

entries.clue: Jovial girl hated the dancing (5-7)

indicatorNotes.dancing: dancers whirl about and swap places, so the letters of 'girl hated the' do the same

annotation.surface: A cheerful girl who nevertheless hated the dancing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jovial girl' reads as a single description, but 'Jovial' stands alone as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe someone cheerful and carefree.

entries.clue: Finished in the short stuff next to the fairway (7)

indicatorNotes.short: 'the' is cut short, losing its last letter

blocks.note: in golf, the rough is the long grass beside the fairway

annotation.surface: A golfer's round ends with the ball in the long grass beside the fairway.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The short stuff' sounds like golf's short grass, but 'short' clips 'the', and the rough is the long stuff.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal sense: someone who is done with a task or a relationship says they are through with it.

entries.clue: Casting starting late is cause of irritation (7)

indicatorNotes.starting late: the word begins one letter later than normal, so its first letter goes

blocks.note: pitching a ball is casting it; its P is then dropped

annotation.surface: A late start to casting a play is annoying the director.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Casting' suggests choosing actors, but it means throwing, as in pitching a ball or fishing line.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the urge to scratch is a kind of skin irritation.

entries.clue: Crass, somewhat bacchanalian affair (4)

indicatorNotes.somewhat: only some of the letters in the phrase are used

blocks.note: the last letter of the first word plus the first three of the second

annotation.surface: A verdict on a vulgar, drunken party.
annotation.walkthrough: NAFF sits across the join, bacchanalia(N AFF)air; it is British slang for tacky or uncool.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: in British slang, naff describes anything tasteless or vulgar.

entries.clue: Be successful with computers and such? Don’t be daft! (4,3,2)

blocks.note: a plan that comes off succeeds
IT = information technology; 'with' just joins the pieces

annotation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of making a fortune out of computing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Come off it!' is a British retort meaning 'don't talk nonsense'.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: both exclamations dismiss what someone has just said as nonsense.

entries.clue: Dismisses employees who take money? (8)

blocks.note: the military verb for throwing an officer out of service

annotation.surface: A firm fires the staff caught pocketing money.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface hints at theft, but the second half is just an innocent description of till staff.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: to cashier an officer is to dismiss them in disgrace, and cashiers are till staff.

entries.clue: Female travelling to their ruby wedding anniversary (8)

indicatorNotes.travelling: things that travel move from where they were, so the letters of 'to their' shift position

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters; 'to' belongs to the fodder

annotation.surface: A woman on her way to celebrate forty years of marriage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'To' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder, supplying the O and one T.
annotation.definitionFit: A traditional naming: each wedding anniversary has a gift material, and ruby marks forty years.

entries.clue: By the way, when agitated, Ann’s a pest! (2,7)

indicatorNotes.when agitated: something agitated is shaken up, so the letters are stirred out of order

annotation.surface: An offhand remark that Ann becomes a nuisance when she's worked up.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is ignored, so its S joins the fodder; 'By the way' opens the surface as an aside.
annotation.definitionFit: A borrowed phrase: French for 'in passing', used in English for a remark made by the way.

entries.clue: List of information absorbed by a US legal representative (6)

indicatorNotes.absorbed by: what is absorbed is soaked up inside, so the first part goes within the second

blocks.note: A + DA, a District Attorney in the US
gen is British slang for information; it goes inside A…DA

annotation.surface: An American lawyer takes in a list of facts.
annotation.walkthrough: GEN, British slang for information, is short for 'general information'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: an agenda is the particular list of items for a meeting.

entries.clue: Mountain in France and North America (4)

indicatorNotes.in France: translate the next word into French

annotation.surface: A mountain found in both France and North America.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface places the mountain in France, but 'in France' only turns 'and' into French.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this Sicilian volcano is one particular mountain.

entries.clue: Inform of a competition reward on the radio (7)

indicatorNotes.on the radio: radio is heard, not seen, so go by sound

blocks.note: a prize is a competition reward

annotation.surface: A radio station announces a contest winner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Inform of' reads as one phrase, and 'of' does double duty since you apprise someone of news.
annotation.definitionFit: A formal synonym: to tell someone about something, usually 'apprise of'.

entries.clue: Lightly-coloured tattoo beneath bottom of hip (4)

indicatorNotes.beneath: in a down clue, INK sits below P
indicatorNotes.bottom of: the bottom of a word is its end, so take the last letter of 'hip'

blocks.note: ink is slang for a tattoo

annotation.surface: A pale tattoo placed low on the hip.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bottom of hip' looks anatomical, but it just means the last letter of the word.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: pink is one pale shade, a light red.

entries.clue: A southern island area where most people live (4)

annotation.surface: A description of a densely populated island in the south.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures one crowded island, but the definition covers a whole continent.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: well over half the world's population lives on this continent.

entries.clue: New route up peak maybe being developed (7)

blocks.note: an ascent is a way up a mountain; 'maybe' because a peak is only one example

annotation.surface: Climbers are working out a new way up a summit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Being developed' reads as describing the route, but it is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something nascent is just coming into being and still taking shape.

entries.clue: Good-natured, socialist family (7)

annotation.surface: A description of a pleasant left-wing household.
annotation.walkthrough: Red has long stood for socialism, from the red flag.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: your kindred are your relatives taken together.

entries.clue: Following a strike, senior journalist is humiliated (7)

indicatorNotes.Following: what follows comes after, so the journalist's letters go after 'a strike'

annotation.surface: After a walkout, the newspaper's editor is left red-faced.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests industrial action, but here it is a blow: a bash.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: to be abashed is to be made to feel ashamed or embarrassed.
